quarter_session_wage_hearings.name: Quarter-Session Wage Hearings
quarter_session_wage_hearings.observation: Four times a year the justices sit at the county town, and a carter paid short may stand before them beside his master.

cloth_workers_guild_demand.name: Cloth Workers' Guild Demand
cloth_workers_guild_demand.observation: The carders and dyers march behind a borrowed banner to the town hall and ask for a hall, a warden and a seal of their own.
cloth_workers_guild_demand.social_consequence: The lesser cloth trades win a voice, and the old guilds see their monopoly contested in the street.

tenant_leagues_against_bondage.name: Tenant Leagues
tenant_leagues_against_bondage.observation: Tenants of twenty villages swear together at the crossroads: no more days at the lord's plough, only a fixed rent in coin.
tenant_leagues_against_bondage.ability_reason: Where tenants hold together, lords must bargain: labor days turn into money rents, and a man's time becomes his own to sell.
tenant_leagues_against_bondage.social_consequence: Lords lose their unpaid ploughmen and answer with bailiffs and gallows; the countryside stays restless for a generation.

board_and_dry_wage_rates.name: Board and Dry Wages
board_and_dry_wage_rates.observation: The mower asks threepence with his dinner or fivepence without, and the farmer reckons which is cheaper this summer.

journeymen_town_boycotts.name: Journeymen's Boycotts
journeymen_town_boycotts.observation: No journeyman saddler will work in the town until the masters raise the day rate, and the brotherhood's letters warn every other town away.
journeymen_town_boycotts.social_consequence: Journeymen learn they can empty a town's workshops; masters learn to fear the brotherhood's letters.

begging_licence_badges.name: Beggars' Badges
begging_licence_badges.observation: The blind and the lame wear the town's pewter badge at the temple door; a sturdy man without one is marched to the ditch works.
begging_licence_badges.social_consequence: The helpless are licensed and fed; the able poor lose the right to ask for bread.

roll_copy_tenure.name: Copyhold Tenure
roll_copy_tenure.observation: The widow keeps her copy of the manor roll in a box: it shows her strips owe four shillings a year and no days at the plough.

demesne_leasing_to_farmers.name: Leased Home Farms
demesne_leasing_to_farmers.observation: The lord's home farm is let to a yeoman for twenty years, and the yeoman hires his own ploughmen by the year.

mining_ordinances.name: Mining Ordinances
mining_ordinances.observation: The mine master reads the ordinance at the shaft head: eight hours a shift, pay every second week, props renewed before any hewing.

mandatory_wander_years.name: Wander Years
mandatory_wander_years.observation: The young cooper shoulders his bundle and walks south; he may not ask for mastership until he has worked in three towns.

eight_hour_mine_shifts.name: Eight-Hour Mine Shifts
eight_hour_mine_shifts.observation: A bell at the shaft head calls the shift up after eight hours; the next crew is already waiting in the changing house.

dawn_hiring_squares.name: Dawn Hiring Squares
dawn_hiring_squares.observation: Before sunrise the day men stand by the fountain with their spades; the builders' foremen pick the strongest and the rest go home.
dawn_hiring_squares.social_consequence: Work is easy to find for the strong and the known; the old and the stranger stand in the square until noon for nothing.

arsenal_sequence_fitting.name: Arsenal Sequence Fitting
arsenal_sequence_fitting.observation: Hulls are towed along the arsenal basin, and from each warehouse window a gang hands down oars, cordage, biscuit or guns in turn.
arsenal_sequence_fitting.ability_reason: One gang at each stage turns a year of shipbuilding into weeks; the state can fit out a fleet between spring and summer.

convict_galley_oarsmen.name: Convict Oarsmen
convict_galley_oarsmen.observation: Thieves and captives sit chained three to a bench; the galley master counts them at dawn and again at dusk.
convict_galley_oarsmen.social_consequence: The galleys never lack rowers, and a sentence to the oar is feared worse than the rope.

off_season_cottage_weaving.name: Winter Cottage Weaving
off_season_cottage_weaving.observation: When the ploughing is done the whole household sits at wheel and loom, and the merchant's cart comes for the cloth at the turn of the year.

statutory_work_hours.name: Statutory Work Hours
statutory_work_hours.observation: From spring to autumn the working day runs dawn to dusk, with half an hour for breakfast and an hour for dinner, and the town bell marks both.

lump_sum_building_contracts.name: Lump-Sum Building Contracts
lump_sum_building_contracts.observation: The master builder signs for the whole guildhall at a fixed price, then hires the masons, carpenters and tilers himself.

permanent_journeymen.name: Permanent Journeymen
permanent_journeymen.observation: At forty the journeyman still sleeps in the master's loft; the mastership fee is more than he will earn in ten years.
permanent_journeymen.social_consequence: A lasting wage class forms inside the guilds, and its brotherhoods grow sharper as hope of mastership fades.

shareholder_wage_miners.name: Shareholders' Wage Miners
shareholder_wage_miners.observation: The townsmen who own the mine shares never go down it; the free miners who once worked their own veins now draw a weekly wage.

wage_books.name: Wage Books
wage_books.observation: Each Saturday the clerk rules a line under the week: days worked, pieces made, pence paid, and the hand makes his mark.

printing_house_crews.name: Printing-House Crews
printing_house_crews.observation: The compositor sets the page, the pressmen pull and ink, the corrector reads the wet proof; two thousand sheets a day leave the house.

export_estate_labor_dues.name: Export Estate Labor Dues
export_estate_labor_dues.observation: The grain ships wait at the river mouth, and on the estates the bailiff demands four days a week at the lord's plough, unpaid.
export_estate_labor_dues.ability_reason: Grain sold abroad makes the lord's own land worth working again, and the cheapest way to work it is to bind the peasants back to it.
export_estate_labor_dues.social_consequence: The estates grow rich on exported grain while their peasants slide back into a bondage the rest of the realm has left behind.

tramping_relief.name: Tramping Relief
tramping_relief.observation: The tramping blacksmith shows his club card at the inn and gets a bed, a supper and word of which town is hiring.

furnace_campaign_crews.name: Furnace Campaign Crews
furnace_campaign_crews.observation: For forty weeks the blast never stops: founders by the hearth, fillers at the throat, colliers in the woods and carters on the roads between.

vagrancy_return_laws.name: Vagrancy Return Laws
vagrancy_return_laws.observation: The constable whips the wanderer at the parish boundary and hands him a pass naming the road home and the days allowed.
vagrancy_return_laws.social_consequence: Parishes keep strangers off their rates, and the poor lose the freedom to go where work might be found.

putting_out_ledgers.name: Putting-Out Ledgers
putting_out_ledgers.observation: The clothier's book lists two hundred spinners by name, the wool weighed out to each and the yarn weighed back.

fathom_bid_contracts.name: Fathom Bid Contracts
fathom_bid_contracts.observation: On bidding day the pairs call their price for each fathom of shaft, and the lowest bid takes the ground for two months.

guild_loom_exclusion.name: Guild Loom Exclusion
guild_loom_exclusion.observation: The weavers' ordinance lets a master's widow keep his loom for a year and a day; any other woman found weaving is fined.
guild_loom_exclusion.social_consequence: Women are pushed from the looms into spinning and the lowest-paid tasks of the cloth trade.

public_work_relief.name: Public Work Relief
public_work_relief.observation: In the hard winter the council sets the idle men to cleaning the moat and paving the market, at a penny under the day rate.

clothier_household_workshops.name: Clothiers' Household Workshops
clothier_household_workshops.observation: The great clothier's house has a hundred looms in its long rooms, and his carders and spinners sleep under the same roof.

overseas_bound_estate_labor.name: Overseas Bound Labor
overseas_bound_estate_labor.observation: The ships carry bound laborers to the new estates by the hundred; the ledgers count them like cargo, and many die before the first harvest.
overseas_bound_estate_labor.ability_reason: Estates in the new lands need hands no free settler will offer; binding laborers and shipping them overseas supplies them, at a terrible price.
overseas_bound_estate_labor.social_consequence: Distant estates prosper on bound hands; the trade poisons the realm's conscience and seeds a long revolt against it.

fewer_holy_days.name: Fewer Holy Days
fewer_holy_days.observation: The new calendar strikes eleven feast days; the ploughman who kept them now works, and the fiddler on the green has fewer dances to play.
fewer_holy_days.social_consequence: Households gain working days and lose the rest and feasting that bound villages together.

compositor_strikes.name: Compositors' Strikes
compositor_strikes.observation: The compositors leave their cases standing half set until the masters grant bread money and a limit on apprentices.

plantation_gang_labor.name: Plantation Gangs
plantation_gang_labor.observation: Under the overseer's whip the gang cuts cane in a line from first light to dark, and the boiling house runs all night.
plantation_gang_labor.social_consequence: The sugar estates yield fortunes to their owners and death to the gangs; the brutality is known, and argued over, at home.

correction_workhouses.name: Houses of Correction
correction_workhouses.observation: Idle men and loose women beat hemp in the house of correction, and the keeper may whip any who will not work.

rotating_mine_drafts.name: Rotating Mine Drafts
rotating_mine_drafts.observation: Each year one man in seven from the subject villages walks to the silver mountain for his draft, and many do not walk back.
rotating_mine_drafts.social_consequence: The silver flows home; the subject villages empty, and their grief becomes a grievance against the realm.

realm_artisan_statute.name: Artisans' Statute
realm_artisan_statute.observation: Every trade in the realm now asks seven years' apprenticeship, and each spring the justices post the wage for mason, thatcher and ploughman.
realm_artisan_statute.ability_reason: One statute for every trade fixes training and pay across the realm: skills become reliable, and every change must wait for the law.
realm_artisan_statute.social_consequence: Masters gain trained hands at fixed wages; laborers lose the right to bargain, and the rules grow harder to change.

compulsory_poor_rate.name: Compulsory Poor Rate
compulsory_poor_rate.observation: Every householder pays the poor rate by the value of his house, and the overseers carry it door to door to the widows and the lame.

acre_rate_harvest_gangs.name: Acre-Rate Harvest Gangs
acre_rate_harvest_gangs.observation: The reapers take the forty acres at a shilling each and work by moonlight to finish before the weather breaks.

bound_colliers.name: Bound Colliers
bound_colliers.observation: A child born at the pit is bound to it, and a collier who leaves may be hauled back like a stolen horse.
bound_colliers.social_consequence: The coal is always hewn; the collier families become a caste apart, despised and unable to leave.

central_manufactory.name: Central Manufactory
central_manufactory.observation: Under one long roof a hundred hands card, spin, weave and shear in turn, each at one step, and the cloth never leaves the building until it is sold.
central_manufactory.ability_reason: Many hands at single steps under one roof let a master watch, time and pay each step; output per hand rises without any new machine.
central_manufactory.social_consequence: Workers gain steady wages and lose control of their hours and their craft; the household workshop begins to dissolve.

parish_poor_law.name: Parish Poor Law
parish_poor_law.observation: Overseers in every parish collect the rate, set the able poor to spinning, feed the helpless and bind pauper children out to masters.
parish_poor_law.ability_reason: A duty to relieve the poor, laid on every parish and paid by a rate, keeps dearth from becoming revolt and gives the state a clerk in every village.
parish_poor_law.social_consequence: No one in the realm is left by law to starve, but the relieved poor lose their liberty, and their children, to the overseers.

company_servant_terms.name: Company Servants
company_servant_terms.observation: The factor signs for seven years at the company's house overseas, on a fixed salary and a promise not to trade on his own account.

poor_work_stock.name: Poor Work Stock
poor_work_stock.observation: The overseers keep a loft of hemp and flax, and any pauper who asks for bread is given a bundle to spin first.

gang_master_harvest_crews.name: Gang-Master Harvest Crews
gang_master_harvest_crews.observation: Every harvest the gang master brings forty reapers over the border hills, and takes a tenth of their pay for the finding.

printed_wage_assessments.name: Printed Wage Assessments
printed_wage_assessments.observation: The printed sheet on the market house door lists the day rate for every trade, with meat and drink and without.

indentured_passage.name: Indentured Passage
indentured_passage.observation: The young weaver signs for four years' service beyond the ocean, and the captain sells his indenture on the quay the day they land.
indentured_passage.social_consequence: The poor buy a passage to new land with their youth; many do not live to finish their term.

lace_schools.name: Lace Schools
lace_schools.observation: Twenty small girls sit at their pillows in the dame's cottage from six years old, and she counts their pins before they may eat.
lace_schools.social_consequence: Families earn from their daughters' fingers, and a generation of girls grows up stooped and half-schooled.

dockyard_task_work.name: Dockyard Task Work
dockyard_task_work.observation: The yard measurer reckons each gang's planking by the foot, and the shipwrights who work fastest take home the most.

commoner_hedge_riots.name: Hedge Riots
commoner_hedge_riots.observation: At night the commoners pull up the new hedges and fill the drainers' ditches, and by morning the cattle are back on the common.
commoner_hedge_riots.social_consequence: Villages hold together against the enclosers, and the magistrates answer with troops and hangings.

corf_piece_rates.name: Corf Piece Rates
corf_piece_rates.observation: Each corf of coal is weighed at the pit head and chalked to the hewer's name, and a light corf is forfeited.

frame_rent_knitters.name: Frame-Rent Knitters
frame_rent_knitters.observation: The knitter pays the hosier ninepence a week for the frame, whether there is work that week or not.
frame_rent_knitters.social_consequence: The hosiers own the frames and the knitters own only their debts.

freeborn_labor_debates.name: Free-Born Debates
freeborn_labor_debates.observation: In the camp tents soldiers and apprentices argue whether a free-born man may be bound to a master, or taxed without his voice.

seamens_articles.name: Seamen's Articles
seamens_articles.observation: Before the ship sails each man signs the articles: his wage by the month, his biscuit and beer by the day, his discharge at the home port.

licensed_numbered_carters.name: Licensed Carters
licensed_numbered_carters.observation: Each cart bears a painted number, and a merchant cheated on the quay can name it to the clerk.

settlement_removal_laws.name: Settlement Removal Laws
settlement_removal_laws.observation: Two justices sign the order, and the pregnant stranger is carted back over the parish line before her child can be born on its rates.
settlement_removal_laws.social_consequence: Parishes guard their rates by expelling the poor; workers dare not move to where wages are higher.

privileged_crown_manufactories.name: Crown Manufactories
privileged_crown_manufactories.observation: The crown's tapestry and mirror works hire foreign masters and local lads alike, and no guild warden may pass its gate.
privileged_crown_manufactories.ability_reason: Works outside guild rules may hire, train and try new methods as they please; the crown pays for skills the guilds would never admit.
privileged_crown_manufactories.social_consequence: Privileged workers earn more than guildsmen and owe everything to the crown; the guilds resent the exemption.

rebuild_trade_opening.name: Open Rebuilding Trades
rebuild_trade_opening.observation: After the fire, any man with a trowel may build in the city for seven years, guild or no guild.

pay_ticket_wages.name: Pay Tickets
pay_ticket_wages.observation: The yard pays in tickets redeemable at quarter day, and the hungry sell theirs to the ticket brokers at a third off.

houses_of_call.name: Houses of Call
houses_of_call.observation: A master tailor short of hands sends his boy to the house of call, where the journeymen sit waiting their turn on the book.

customary_perquisites.name: Customary Perquisites
customary_perquisites.observation: Each shipwright walks out of the yard at evening with a bundle of chips on his shoulder, his by a custom as old as the yard.

crown_works_settlements.name: Crown Works Settlements
crown_works_settlements.observation: Beside the royal glassworks stand rows of workers' lodgings, a bakehouse and a school, all paid from the works' account.

recruited_foreign_craftsmen.name: Recruited Foreign Craftsmen
recruited_foreign_craftsmen.observation: The company pays the passage of twelve foreign glass grinders and houses them on a street the townsfolk soon name for their tongue.

friendly_society_boxes.name: Friendly Society Boxes
friendly_society_boxes.observation: Every Saturday night at the inn each member drops his pennies into the box with three locks, and a sick member draws from it.

seamens_hospital_levy.name: Seamen's Hospital Levy
seamens_hospital_levy.observation: Sixpence a month comes off every sailor's pay for the great hospital by the river, where the crippled of the fleet end their days.

coal_river_strikes.name: Coal River Strikes
coal_river_strikes.observation: The keelmen moor their boats across the river, and no coal goes down to the ships until the fitters raise the rate.

spinning_schools.name: Spinning Schools
spinning_schools.observation: The parish spinning school takes pauper children at seven; they spin from six to six and are fed on what their yarn earns.
spinning_schools.social_consequence: Pauper children are fed and taught a trade, and their childhood is spent at the wheel.

family_moulder_gangs.name: Family Moulder Gangs
family_moulder_gangs.observation: The moulder is paid by the thousand; his wife tempers the clay and his children carry the wet bricks to the drying hacks.

loom_shop_cottages.name: Loom-Shop Cottages
loom_shop_cottages.observation: The weaver's cottage has a long window upstairs to light three looms, and the family lives in the room below.

mill_hand_workforce.name: Mill Hands
mill_hand_workforce.observation: When the mill bell rings, three hundred hands file in to tend the water-driven throwing machines, and the gate shuts behind the last.
mill_hand_workforce.ability_reason: Machines driven by one wheel need tenders, not spinners: once the bell and the gate hold a workforce together, one hand can mind many spindles.
mill_hand_workforce.social_consequence: Wages are steady, but the bell rules the day, children tend machines beside their parents, and the household workshop empties.

artisan_emigration_bans.name: Artisan Emigration Bans
artisan_emigration_bans.observation: A clockmaker caught on a foreign-bound ship with his tools is fined and sent home, and his tools are forfeit.

workhouse_test.name: Workhouse Test
workhouse_test.observation: The overseers offer relief only inside the workhouse; most of the hungry look at its gate and go back to the road.
workhouse_test.social_consequence: The rates fall, and the poor learn to dread the house more than hunger.

town_wide_combinations.name: Town-Wide Combinations
town_wide_combinations.observation: The journeymen of every tailor's shop in town meet at one tavern and send a single petition: a shilling more and an hour less.

saint_monday_custom.name: Idle Monday
saint_monday_custom.observation: On Monday the cutlers' wheels stand still; the grinders drink and play at skittles, and make up the week by working all Friday night.

servant_register_offices.name: Servant Register Offices
servant_register_offices.observation: For a shilling the register office writes down a cook's character and her last place, and sends her to a lady who needs one.

gauged_piece_tickets.name: Gauged Piece Tickets
gauged_piece_tickets.observation: The nailer's work is checked against the brass gauge before the ticket is written, and short nails are paid at half.

mine_shift_registers.name: Mine Shift Registers
mine_shift_registers.observation: The overman writes in the daily book who went down, which heading each worked and how many tubs came up.

perquisite_strikes.name: Chip Strikes
perquisite_strikes.observation: When the yard forbids chips, the shipwrights down tools and march to the navy office gate with bundles on their shoulders.

pin_shop_division.name: Pin Shop Division
pin_shop_division.observation: One man draws the wire, another straightens it, a third cuts, a fourth points, and ten together make pins by the tens of thousands a day.

yearly_pitmen_bond.name: Yearly Pitmen's Bond
yearly_pitmen_bond.observation: On binding day each pitman takes the bounty money and signs for a year; he may not leave the colliery until the next binding.

navvy_gangs.name: Travelling Diggers
navvy_gangs.observation: The diggers come with their barrows and planks and camp by the new cut, and the villages bar their doors when the gang is paid.

strike_funds.name: Strike Funds
strike_funds.observation: Each weaver pays a penny a week into the common box, and when the masters cut the price the box keeps the looms idle for a month.

wage_assessment_lapse.name: Wage Assessments Lapse
wage_assessment_lapse.observation: The justices no longer post a wage; the farmer and the mower settle it between them at the gate.

factory_shift_system.name: Factory Shifts
factory_shift_system.observation: The mill clock rings at six in the morning and six at night; one shift leaves the frames warm for the next, and the wheel never stops.
factory_shift_system.ability_reason: Machines run round the clock only if people do; two shifts double what one water wheel can spin.
factory_shift_system.social_consequence: Night work, children at the frames and fines for a minute's lateness become ordinary.

landless_wage_laborers.name: Landless Laborers
landless_wage_laborers.observation: The common is hedged and the cottager's cow is sold; now he and his sons take whatever work the farmer offers, by the day.
landless_wage_laborers.ability_reason: Enclosed farms need fewer hands, and the hands they shed must sell their labor: a mobile wage workforce appears for the mills and the towns.
landless_wage_laborers.social_consequence: The farms grow more; the cottagers lose their cow, their fuel and their independence.

statutory_price_lists.name: Statutory Price Lists
statutory_price_lists.observation: The justices seal the weavers' list: so much for a plain piece of forty yards, so much more for a figured one, throughout the valley.

factory_villages.name: Factory Villages
factory_villages.observation: The mill owner builds three rows of stone cottages, a chapel and a shop that takes his own tokens.
factory_villages.social_consequence: Mill families get sound houses, and the master owns their roof, their shop and their Sunday.

trade_freedom_edict.name: Trade Freedom Edict
trade_freedom_edict.observation: The edict is read in every guildhall: any man may take up any trade, and the wardens' seals are void.
trade_freedom_edict.ability_reason: With the guild monopolies gone, anyone may try a trade or a new method, and skill moves to where it is paid best.
trade_freedom_edict.social_consequence: Newcomers and innovators flourish; old masters lose their privileges, and journeymen the brotherhoods that sheltered them.

division_of_labor_doctrine.name: Division of Labor Doctrine
division_of_labor_doctrine.observation: The professor's book argues that the realm grows rich not by hoarding gold but by splitting work into many small, practised tasks.

pauper_mill_apprentices.name: Pauper Mill Apprentices
pauper_mill_apprentices.observation: A wagon carries twenty parish children up the valley to the mill, bound until twenty-one, and the parish is glad to be rid of the cost.
pauper_mill_apprentices.social_consequence: The mills get cheap hands in remote valleys; the children grow up bent and unschooled, far from anyone who knew them.

machine_breaking_riots.name: Machine Breaking
machine_breaking_riots.observation: Masked shearmen break into the finishing shop at night and smash the new shearing frames with great hammers.
machine_breaking_riots.social_consequence: Hand workers fight for their living; masters hesitate to install machines, and the state sends soldiers to the valleys.

worker_pass_books.name: Workers' Pass-Books
worker_pass_books.observation: No master may hire a journeyman whose book lacks his last master's signature and the date he left.

factory_fine_rules.name: Mill Fine Rules
factory_fine_rules.observation: The board by the gate lists the fines: a penny for talking, twopence for an open window, a morning's pay for coming after the bell.

bound_labor_abolition_movement.name: Abolition Societies
bound_labor_abolition_movement.observation: The society's petition carries eighty thousand names, and its pamphlets print the plan of a ship packed with bound captives.
bound_labor_abolition_movement.ability_reason: Petitions and pamphlets turn a distant trade into a moral question at home; the realm can choose to end what enriches it.
bound_labor_abolition_movement.social_consequence: Ordinary people sign against a trade their merchants profit from; the planters and their allies fight every step.

estate_bondage_abolition.name: Bondage Abolished
estate_bondage_abolition.observation: The decree is read at the manor gate: no more days at the lord's plough, and any tenant may marry, move or learn a trade without leave.
estate_bondage_abolition.ability_reason: Free tenants go where labor pays and improve land they cannot lose; the estates must hire or rent instead of command.
estate_bondage_abolition.social_consequence: Peasants gain their persons; lords lose unpaid labor and demand compensation that burdens the freed for decades.

registered_friendly_societies.name: Registered Friendly Societies
registered_friendly_societies.observation: The society's rules are lodged with the clerk of the peace, and a treasurer who runs off with the box can now be sued.

bread_scale_wage_supplements.name: Bread-Scale Supplements
bread_scale_wage_supplements.observation: The justices' table sets what a laborer with three children needs by the price of the loaf, and the parish pays the gap.
bread_scale_wage_supplements.social_consequence: No family starves when bread is dear, but farmers pay starvation wages knowing the rate will make them up.

general_combination_ban.name: Combination Ban
general_combination_ban.observation: Two journeymen who meet to talk of wages may now be jailed for three months on one justice's word.
general_combination_ban.social_consequence: Masters and magistrates break the workers' clubs, which go underground, swear secret oaths and grow more bitter.

collier_bond_release.name: Colliers Released
collier_bond_release.observation: The statute is read at the pit head: colliers' children are born free, and no collier may be hauled back to a pit he has left.
